packs.name: @atlante/pack
packs.readmeHtml:
@atlante/pack

Atlante's first-party static pack gives a project a useful default agent and skills for deliberate AI-assisted work. It provides the architect agent, the four delivery-phase skills brainstorm, plan, build, and review, the additional non-phase harness stewardship skill, and reusable templates and instances for composing your own agents, skills, workflows, and supporting prompt content.

Default usage

Initialize a project with the first-party pack:

npx atlante@latest init

The CLI selects the default preset from @atlante/pack and writes "extends": "@atlante/pack" to atlante.jsonc, then materializes the initial native outputs. The default initialization path resolves the pack from the CLI installation, so it does not require a separate @atlante/pack installation.

Explicit usage

Install the pack when a project-authored configuration references it directly:

npm install --save-dev @atlante/pack

Then extend the preset and select a reusable template in atlante.jsonc:

{
  "$schema": "https://atlante.sh/schema/v0.1/schema.json",
  "extends": "@atlante/pack",
  "values": {
    "project": "my-app",
  },
  "agents": {
    // A project-specific agent: the preset already provides the
    // general-purpose architect, so add the roles your project needs.
    "migration-writer": {
      "$template": "@atlante/pack/agent",
      "description": "Writes and reviews schema migrations for {{values.project}}.",
      "identity": "You are the migration specialist on {{values.project}}.",
      "mission": "Ship safe, reversible, and tested schema migrations.",
      "sections": [
        {
          "responsibilities": [
            "Write forward and rollback migrations for schema changes",
            "Review migrations for data-loss risks before they merge",
          ],
        },
        {
          "invariants": ["Every migration ships with a tested rollback path."],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
}

extends selects a preset. $template selects a template, whose input schema defines the remaining fields for that agent or skill. Local configuration takes precedence over the inherited preset.

Workflow

@atlante/pack/workflow provides a generic ordered prose-workflow template and a concrete first-party instance. The generic template accepts only non-empty phases, each with a name, non-empty instructions, and an optional artifact output. It renders the phases in configured order but does not execute or enforce them.

The concrete instance defines Brainstorm, Plan, Build, and Review. The architect decides which phases materially improve the result, preserves the order among the selected phases, and treats the phases and skills as guidance. Plan and Review have persistent artifact paths rooted at {{values.workflow-root}}; the preset default is .atlante/workflows, and projects may override it. Brainstorm and Build outputs do not have file paths. Review explicitly supports task-level and final review boundaries, and Build/Review corrections are bounded to five rounds per task by the instance prose, not by template or runtime enforcement. Checkpoints are project-approved reviewable change boundaries, not automatically Git commits.

Contents

Useful public locators include:

Category Locators
Default preset @atlante/pack
Agent instance @atlante/pack/architect
Phase skill instances @atlante/pack/brainstorm, @atlante/pack/plan, @atlante/pack/build, @atlante/pack/review
Stewardship skill instance @atlante/pack/harness
Agent and skill templates @atlante/pack/agent, @atlante/pack/skill
Supporting templates @atlante/pack/workflow, @atlante/pack/markdown, @atlante/pack/artifact, @atlante/pack/gotchas, @atlante/pack/instructions, @atlante/pack/responsibilities, @atlante/pack/invariants, @atlante/pack/references

The default preset exposes exactly one agent binding, architect, and five public skill bindings: the four delivery-phase skills brainstorm, plan, build, and review, plus the non-phase harness stewardship skill. The workflow instance's phases reference the four phase skills, and the architect selects the phases and skills that materially improve the result. The skill bindings are locator-only, so each skill instance owns its description. The agent template requires identity and mission; both agent and skill templates support ordered markdown, instructions, responsibilities, gotchas, workflow, and invariants sections. The skill template also supports references sections, which render named entries with their locations and optional read-when guidance. Responsibilities name owned outcomes, while instructions describe ordered actions and invariants carry binding guarantees and approval gates.

Harness stewardship

@atlante/pack/harness is not a workflow phase. It carries the conditional operational guidance for initializing, configuring, validating, building, troubleshooting, and improving an Atlante harness, and the architect prompt routes harness-touching work to it alongside the active phase skills — it supplements them rather than replacing them. The skill keeps permanent policy (concepts, resource selection, the source-versus-generated boundary, and the separately approved harness-improvement cycle) authoritative and treats command-level mechanics as provisional, so deterministic tools can absorb the mechanics later without changing the policy. Harness changes always require explicit developer approval and run as their own delivery cycle.

Pack behavior

The @atlante/pack/markdown template expects an ordered block array, not a string. This is a breaking change for authored configurations that used the old form: rewrite { "markdown": "Body" } as { "markdown": [{ "p": ["Body"] }] } before upgrading to a release that contains this block-array change.

This is a static pack with atlante.format: 1; it has no runtime JavaScript entry point. Atlante loads only the selected template or instance and its transitive dependencies. It does not scan installed packages or install dependencies, so direct project references must be declared and installed by the project's package manager.

# `@atlante/pack`

Atlante's first-party static pack gives a project a useful default agent and
skills for deliberate AI-assisted work. It provides the `architect` agent, the
four delivery-phase skills `brainstorm`, `plan`, `build`, and `review`, the
additional non-phase `harness` stewardship skill, and reusable templates and
instances for composing your own agents, skills, workflows, and supporting
prompt content.

## Default usage

Initialize a project with the first-party pack:

```bash
npx atlante@latest init
```

The CLI selects the default preset from `@atlante/pack` and writes
`"extends": "@atlante/pack"` to `atlante.jsonc`, then materializes the initial
native outputs. The default initialization path resolves the pack from the CLI
installation, so it does not require a separate `@atlante/pack` installation.

## Explicit usage

Install the pack when a project-authored configuration references it directly:

```bash
npm install --save-dev @atlante/pack
```

Then extend the preset and select a reusable template in `atlante.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://atlante.sh/schema/v0.1/schema.json",
  "extends": "@atlante/pack",
  "values": {
    "project": "my-app",
  },
  "agents": {
    // A project-specific agent: the preset already provides the
    // general-purpose architect, so add the roles your project needs.
    "migration-writer": {
      "$template": "@atlante/pack/agent",
      "description": "Writes and reviews schema migrations for {{values.project}}.",
      "identity": "You are the migration specialist on {{values.project}}.",
      "mission": "Ship safe, reversible, and tested schema migrations.",
      "sections": [
        {
          "responsibilities": [
            "Write forward and rollback migrations for schema changes",
            "Review migrations for data-loss risks before they merge",
          ],
        },
        {
          "invariants": ["Every migration ships with a tested rollback path."],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
}
```

`extends` selects a preset. `$template` selects a template, whose input
schema defines the remaining fields for that agent or skill. Local
configuration takes precedence over the inherited preset.

## Workflow

`@atlante/pack/workflow` provides a generic ordered prose-workflow template and
a concrete first-party instance. The generic template accepts only non-empty
`phases`, each with a `name`, non-empty `instructions`, and an optional
artifact `output`. It renders the phases in configured order but does not
execute or enforce them.

The concrete instance defines `Brainstorm`, `Plan`, `Build`, and `Review`. The
architect decides which phases materially improve the result, preserves the
order among the selected phases, and treats the phases and skills as guidance.
`Plan` and `Review` have persistent artifact paths rooted at
`{{values.workflow-root}}`; the preset default is `.atlante/workflows`, and
projects may override it. `Brainstorm` and `Build` outputs do not have file
paths. `Review` explicitly supports task-level and final review boundaries,
and Build/Review corrections are bounded to five rounds per task by the
instance prose, not by template or runtime enforcement. Checkpoints are
project-approved reviewable change boundaries, not automatically Git commits.

## Contents

Useful public locators include:

| Category | Locators |
| --- | --- |
| Default preset | `@atlante/pack` |
| Agent instance | `@atlante/pack/architect` |
| Phase skill instances | `@atlante/pack/brainstorm`, `@atlante/pack/plan`, `@atlante/pack/build`, `@atlante/pack/review` |
| Stewardship skill instance | `@atlante/pack/harness` |
| Agent and skill templates | `@atlante/pack/agent`, `@atlante/pack/skill` |
| Supporting templates | `@atlante/pack/workflow`, `@atlante/pack/markdown`, `@atlante/pack/artifact`, `@atlante/pack/gotchas`, `@atlante/pack/instructions`, `@atlante/pack/responsibilities`, `@atlante/pack/invariants`, `@atlante/pack/references` |

The default preset exposes exactly one agent binding, `architect`, and five
public skill bindings: the four delivery-phase skills `brainstorm`, `plan`,
`build`, and `review`, plus the non-phase `harness` stewardship skill. The
workflow instance's phases reference the four phase skills, and the architect
selects the phases and skills that materially improve the result. The skill
bindings are locator-only, so each skill instance owns its description. The
agent template requires `identity` and `mission`; both agent and skill templates
support ordered `markdown`, `instructions`, `responsibilities`, `gotchas`,
`workflow`, and `invariants` sections. The skill template also supports
`references` sections, which render named entries with their locations and
optional read-when guidance.
Responsibilities name owned outcomes, while instructions describe ordered
actions and invariants carry binding guarantees and approval gates.

## Harness stewardship

`@atlante/pack/harness` is not a workflow phase. It carries the conditional
operational guidance for initializing, configuring, validating, building,
troubleshooting, and improving an Atlante harness, and the architect prompt
routes harness-touching work to it alongside the active phase skills — it
supplements them rather than replacing them. The skill keeps permanent policy
(concepts, resource selection, the source-versus-generated boundary, and the
separately approved harness-improvement cycle) authoritative and treats
command-level mechanics as provisional, so deterministic tools can absorb the
mechanics later without changing the policy. Harness changes always require
explicit developer approval and run as their own delivery cycle.

## Pack behavior

The `@atlante/pack/markdown` template expects an ordered block array, not a
string. This is a breaking change for authored configurations that used the old
form: rewrite `{ "markdown": "Body" }` as
`{ "markdown": [{ "p": ["Body"] }] }` before upgrading to a release that
contains this block-array change.

This is a static pack with `atlante.format: 1`; it has no runtime
JavaScript entry point. Atlante loads only the selected template or instance
and its transitive dependencies. It does not scan installed packages or install
dependencies, so direct project references must be declared and installed by
the project's package manager.

{
  "$template": "@atlante/pack/skill",
  "description": "Use when a defined task is ready for implementation: make the smallest verified change that satisfies its acceptance criteria.",
  "title": "Build",
  "overview": "Implement one defined task through focused test feedback and return the change with truthful validation evidence.",
  "sections": [
    {
      "instructions": [
        "Read the complete task definition, its acceptance criteria, applicable project instructions, and the relevant source and tests before editing.",
        "Identify the observable outcome, affected invariants, and exact scope; if any of them is materially unclear or blocked, stop and report it before changing code.",
        "For a bug or unexpected failure, reproduce it and trace the root cause before proposing a fix; test one hypothesis at a time and fix the source rather than the symptom.",
        "Before writing the test body, name the regression it must catch; exercise observable behavior through real code, using mocks only at unavoidable slow or external boundaries.",
        "For a behavior change, write the smallest focused test that expresses the expected behavior and run it before implementation.",
        "Confirm that the focused test fails for the expected reason; if it already passes or fails for an unrelated reason, investigate, revise the test, or return evidence that the task assumption is wrong instead of proceeding under a false red state.",
        "Make the smallest implementation that satisfies the focused test and demonstrates it passing.",
        "Add meaningful boundary and failure cases around the changed behavior, then record what each relevant test proves.",
        "For a change without an observable behavior difference, explain why red-green feedback is not meaningful and use the strongest relevant verification instead of manufacturing an artificial test.",
        "When a task addresses review findings, read the complete review context and verify every finding against the actual code and defined scope; if a finding is unclear, technically unsound, or conflicts with the contract, report the evidence instead of implementing it blindly.",
        "Address every valid required change within scope, and describe the resulting current state rather than only the latest change.",
        "Immediately before claiming completion, run the full commands that prove each claim, read their complete output and exit status, and report the actual results; stale, partial, or unavailable evidence is not a pass.",
        "Before returning the result, inspect the actual diff and confirm that it matches the defined scope, preserves unrelated changes, satisfies every acceptance criterion, and contains no accidental or unsupported edits.",
        "Return a concise implementation handoff containing the scope, decisions, changed files, acceptance evidence, validation evidence, and any concerns or blockers."
      ]
    },
    {
      "invariants": [
        "Work on exactly one defined task; MUST NOT absorb adjacent scope or weaken the requested outcome.",
        "MUST NOT implement a behavior change until its focused test has produced the expected red evidence, and MUST NOT manufacture tests for non-behavior changes.",
        "MUST preserve unrelated work and keep it distinct from the implemented change.",
        "MUST reuse or extend suitable existing code before creating a new implementation, keeping responsibility boundaries intact; extract shared code only for real duplication or multiple concrete consumers, and MUST NOT introduce speculative generalization.",
        "MUST NOT claim completion until the acceptance criteria and required checks are satisfied with reported evidence.",
        "When required context, access, or validation is unavailable, MUST stop at the smallest safe point and report the blocker instead of improvising."
      ]
    }
  ]
}

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "A list of situational failure-mode reminders that help the agent avoid common mistakes.",
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
  "minItems": 1
}

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "An ordered instruction list.",
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
  "minItems": 1
}

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "Conditions that MUST remain true throughout the work. Keep the set minimal and focused; include only consequential rules that must hold continuously. Use invariants for durable guarantees, safety boundaries, and approval gates. State each as one concrete, observable rule and include the compliant path when non-obvious. Back critical invariants with deterministic enforcement when possible. Use instructions for ordered actions, responsibilities for owned outcomes, and gotchas for situational risks. Do not duplicate requirements across sections.",
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
  "minItems": 1
}

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "Positive, ongoing outcomes owned throughout the work. Use responsibilities for what must be accomplished, not for behavioral limits; behavioral limits and approval gates belong in invariants. Do not duplicate requirements across sections.",
  "type": "array",
  "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
  "minItems": 1
}

{
  "$template": "@atlante/pack/skill",
  "description": "Use when an implementation needs independent inspection: verify the requested change against its requirements and return an evidence-based verdict.",
  "title": "Review",
  "overview": "Inspect a focused task change or a complete change set without modifying it, then report actionable findings and a truthful verdict.",
  "sections": [
    {
      "instructions": [
        "Read the complete review request, defined scope and acceptance criteria, applicable project instructions, supplied change boundary, and available validation evidence before forming conclusions.",
        "Establish the actual reviewed boundary from source control and the working tree, identifying changed files, included uncommitted work, excluded unrelated changes, and generated outputs.",
        "Inspect the actual source, diff, and tests yourself; use summaries only for orientation and verify every material claim against primary evidence.",
        "Scale investigation depth to the complexity, risk, and uncertainty of the change, but MUST NOT omit direct source inspection, acceptance verification, or the evidence needed to support the verdict.",
        "For a focused task review, inspect the changed behavior and its immediate integration boundary; for a whole-change review, inspect the complete change set and cross-task interactions. Inspect outside that boundary only to evaluate a concrete risk you can name, and record both the risk and what you inspected.",
        "Assess acceptance compliance explicitly: identify anything missing, extra, misunderstood, or unverifiable, and distinguish implementation defects from ambiguity or defects in the requirements themselves.",
        "For a correction re-review, verify each prior finding against the correction boundary and inspect that boundary for newly introduced breakage; MUST NOT reopen unaffected code, and report unrelated observations as non-blocking and out of scope.",
        "Review correctness, acceptance compliance, regressions, compatibility, security, maintainability, and test quality; distinguish introduced defects from pre-existing or out-of-scope observations.",
        "Evaluate supplied validation evidence for completeness and consistency before running commands. Run only the focused checks needed to verify acceptance, investigate a concrete doubt, or close an evidence gap; SHOULD NOT repeat broad validation when sufficient evidence already exists. Report supplied evidence separately from checks run directly, including their results and limitations.",
        "Record each finding as `critical`, `important`, or `minor` with an exact location, evidence, impact, and required correction; omit speculative concerns and optional style preferences.",
        "Return a report containing the reviewed boundary, acceptance assessment, commands and results, findings grouped by severity, pre-existing or out-of-scope observations, limitations, and a `PASS` or `BLOCKED` verdict.",
        "For a correction re-review, include an `ADDRESSED` or `NOT ADDRESSED` verdict with evidence for each prior finding.",
        "Before returning the report, check that every finding is supported by evidence, severities match impact, required corrections are actionable, and the verdict agrees with the findings and check results."
      ]
    },
    {
      "invariants": [
        "MUST NOT intentionally modify reviewed source, configuration, or tests, and MUST NOT correct findings yourself; return the review report only.",
        "MUST NOT trust summaries or reported validation without reconciling them against the actual change and primary evidence.",
        "MUST NOT report a finding without exact evidence, impact, and a required correction, and MUST NOT suppress a valid finding for convenience.",
        "MUST NOT present supplied validation as independently verified, claim that an unperformed check passed, or return `PASS` when evidence required to substantiate acceptance is missing.",
        "Any unresolved critical or important finding or failed required check MUST make the verdict `BLOCKED`."
      ]
    }
  ]
}
